timelineEvents.title: Legal Permanent Entry
timelineEvents.label: 1 Nov 1935 · Permanent U.S. entry
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper enters the United States for permanent residence through Calexico with Eleonora.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Enters for permanent residence at Calexico, California, from Mexicali on 1 November 1935, travelling on foot with Eleonora. The manifest records 6626 Franklin Ave., Hollywood, as his U.S. destination; his Declaration of Intention four months later records the same address as his residence.

places.publicNote: U.S. border city and port-of-entry context for Kaper’s 1935 permanent-residence entry record.

Mexicali is the Baja California border city from which Kaper and Eleonora entered the United States at Calexico for permanent residence. The map marker uses official city-level coordinates and does not identify the location of the historical Commercial Hotel.

places.displayName: Château des Fleurs, 6626 Franklin Ave., Hollywood
places.authorizedName: Château des Fleurs, 6626 Franklin Avenue, Hollywood, Los Angeles
places.publicNote: French Norman Revival apartment building completed in 1927 and designated Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument no. 799. Kaper’s 1 November 1935 immigration manifest records 6626 Franklin Avenue as his U.S. destination, and his Declaration of Intention dated 4 February 1936 records the same address as his residence.

places.displayName: Commercial Hotel (formerly Hotel Aldrete), Madero at Azueta, Mexicali
places.authorizedName: Hotel Comercial (formerly Hotel Aldrete), Avenida Francisco I. Madero at Calle José Azueta, Mexicali, Baja California
places.publicNote: Kaper’s 1 November 1935 Calexico manifest records the Commercial Hotel in Mexicali as his last permanent residence abroad. Historical evidence identifies the Hotel Comercial as the renamed Hotel Aldrete on Avenida Francisco I. Madero, between Ayuntamiento and José Azueta, beside Parque Héroes de Chapultepec. The marker represents that documented site; 301 is the present-day parcel number, not a verified 1935 street number.

places.authorizedName: Calexico–Mexicali Port of Entry (Calexico, California / Mexicali, Baja California)
places.publicNote: Land border port of entry linking Calexico (California) and Mexicali (Baja California), documented as the point of Kaper and Eleonora’s 1935 permanent-residence entry into the United States. The coordinates mark the historic downtown crossing at the foot of Heffernan Avenue, where the 1933 inspection station stood in 1935; the vehicle crossing was moved two blocks west in 1974 and the present buildings are later.
